checks: The positive projective chart preserves actual fibers and convex hulls, and closed cap traces pull back to closed cap traces. Unweighted image volume pulls back with factor L(p)^(-d), from scaling the d continuous coordinates only.

The chart preserves every convex trace of the finite base and its Helly number. Normalized nonnegative affine arrays form a compact simplex section. On the positive part finite fiber densities vary continuously in total variation, so the maximum depth is continuous on the fixed sample.

For fixed normal the through-cap mass is upper semicontinuous in the mark, by the closed threshold indicator. The infimum over normals remains upper semicontinuous and attains its maximum on the compact sample.

At a boundary array the zero set is a proper exposed-face trace. Its weights diverge and outside weights remain bounded. The restricted transformed family is actual with fewer sites. Intrinsic containing cuts extend to ambient cuts, and face traces lift to traces on the whole base, proving the stated depth and Helly inequalities.
The strict gap at L=1 excludes boundary limits of minimizing sequences. Interior continuity gives attainment and affine-denominator composition gives the claimed local orbit minimality.
